newsitem.title: USA: Rains continue to limit fieldwork for U.S. cotton.
newsitem.headline: Rains continue to limit fieldwork for U.S. cotton.

text.p: Rain was once again a deterrent for fieldwork on cotton crops in U.S. producer states, according to weekly crop reports from the National Agricultural Statistics Service. Insect prblems may have helped keep development slightly behind schedule in some areas.

MISSISSIPPI - According to the Mississippi Agricultural Statistics Service, there were 3.2 days suitable for fieldwork for the week ending June 22, 1997. Cotton producers are anticipating pin head applications. Soil moisture conditions were rated 2 percent short, 55 percent adequate and 43 percent surplus.

Cotton crop progress was 100 percent emerged versus 99 percent last week, 100 percent last year, and 100 percent on a 5 year average. Squaring was rated 32 percent this week versus 7 percent last week, 88 percent last year, and 70 percent on average.
Crop conditions were rated 5 percent excellent, 26 percent good, 44 percent fair, 18 percent poor and 7 percent very poor.

GEORGIA - Rains fell over much of the state this week, according to the Georgia Agricultural Statistics Service. Showers added to already saturated fields further delaying field activities. Soil moisture levels on Friday were rated 96 percent adequate or surplus, the highest since early May. Field work was also slowed by weather conditions in the major row crop areas.

Cotton development is still several days behind normal, but with warmer temperatures, cotton development should accelerate. County Extension Officials reported 3.8 days suitable for fieldwork. Other activities included spraying for diseases, weed control in row crops and cotton scouting.
Crops were rated 42 percent squared versus 26 percent last week, 64 percent last year, and 57 percent on average.
Crop conditions were rated 8 percent excellent, 56 percent good, 31 percent fair, and 5 percent poor.

LOUISIANA - Heavy rains mid-week brought field activities to a halt throughout the state. According to reports, there were 3.7 days suitable for fieldwork. Soil moisture was rated 6 percent short, 54 percent adequate and 40 percent surplus.

Crop conditions were rated 3 percent excellent, 49 percent good, 41 percent fair, and 7 percent poor. Squaring was rated at 88 percent, versus 18 percent last week, 83 percent last year and 71 percent on average.
Cotton growers reported light to moderate infestations of boll weevils.

TEXAS - A return to warmer, open conditions by mid-week was a welcomed relief for producers in most areas of the state. Early week storms in the Plains caused some damage. The warmer temperatures aided growth and maturing of crops.

Insect problems continued in many fields. Plants were beginning to set bolls in the Blacklands and Central Texas. Progress was also good in the Coastal Bend and Rio Grande Valley where bolls were setting. Spraying activity also continued in these areas. Statewide cotton conditions were rated at 70 percent of normal compared with 52 percent last year.

Cotton was 98 percent planted versus 93 percent last week, 95 percent last year and 95 percent on average. Squaring was rated at 28 percent versus 16 percent last week, 31 percent last year and 27 percent on average. Crop conditions were 9 percent excellent, 43 percent good, 29 percent fair, 13 percent poor and 6 percent very poor.

CALIFORNIA - Field activities made good progress under favorable weather conditions in most areas of the state, according to California Agricultural Statistics Service. Cotton was cultivated, irrigated, and treated for aphids, lygus, mites and weeds. Growth and development were excellent in most areas, with some fields three weeks ahead of normal progress.

ARIZONA - Temperatures were closer to normal this week as average temperatures ranged from 4 degrees below normal to 1 degree above normal statewide. Cotton continued to set bolls in the western part of the State while fields in the east were still in the squaring stage. Overall, 32 percent of the crop was setting bolls compared to 31 percent last year and 24 percent on average. Crop conditions rated 32 percent excellent, 53 percent good, 11 percent fair, 3 percent poor and 1 percent very poor.
